Customer Support Dashboard — Frontend QA Audit

Project: Harbor & Thread Support (React 19 · React Router 7 · Tailwind 4 · Vite 8) · Audited 2026-10-27 · Review only: no application source was modified

34findings
0Critical
6High
19Medium
9Low
68checks run (64 in a live browser)

1 · Executive summary

Bottom line: the dashboard is a well-built, visually consistent small-team support tool whose core ticket workflow (reply, note, assign, prioritise, resolve, reopen, escalate to developers) works and stays consistent across the sidebar badge, status tabs, dashboard and analytics. Lint and typecheck are clean and the console shows one error (a missing favicon). It is not yet ready to present unaided: a visitor cannot sign in without a private note, the header search breaks while typing, and the ticket screen is unusable on a phone.

Fix before presenting (P0): F-01 undocumented sign-in · F-02 header search loses focus · F-26 ticket detail unusable at 390 px. All three are small-to-medium changes.

What is genuinely missing

  1. Triage visibility. Inbox rows hide priority, status and assignee, and no view lists overdue, unassigned or awaiting-response tickets (F-18, F-03, F-09).
  2. Customer and order context inside the ticket (F-08); the data exists on the Customers page and in seed orders.
  3. Reliable demo data: seed times drift with the browser and there is no reset (F-06); several seeds contradict themselves (F-07).
  4. Search that matches how stores work: order numbers and email (F-05).
  5. Connected secondary systems: notifications and many Settings controls are decoration (F-12, F-13), and Analytics cannot show a response-time trend (F-15).

What is already good (no change needed)

Ticket lifecycle and validation, internal notes, the escalation hand-off to developers, role rules (lead vs agent), agent removal safeguards and reassignment, settings validation and persistence, corrupted-storage fallback, URL-based inbox filters, empty states, and metric definitions shared through lib/metrics.ts. The visual direction (warm canvas, sage accent, floating sidebar) is coherent and should be kept.

How this audit was done

  • Code inspection: every file under src/ (3,676 lines in 34 files), config and package files.
  • Runtime: the Vite dev server (read only) opened in a separate headless Chrome 154 driven through the DevTools protocol. Test probes and the report generator live in the session scratchpad, not in the project. The shared browser profile of the usual MCP browser was locked by another session, so the built-in screenshot tools were not used; all screenshots were captured from the live app by that Chrome.
  • Not touched: application source, tests, config and lockfiles. The only files created are under docs/audit/. No production build was run, because npm run build would overwrite dist/.
  • Evidence labels: each finding says whether it was confirmed at runtime, computed, or based on code only. One scenario (data drift, F-06) is a simulation: I shifted persisted timestamps back three days rather than waiting three days.

Functional and data findings

F-01

Reviewers cannot sign in: credentials are undocumented

HighConfirmedP0
Category
Functional
Location
src/pages/LoginPage.tsx, src/data/seed.ts:34-46, README.md
Current behavior
The app opens on a bare Sign in form (email, password, button). The page text is only the workspace name. Every seeded agent shares one SHA-256 password hash. Nothing on the page, in the README or in the repo says which email or password to use. The README is still the unmodified Vite template.
Evidence
Runtime: loaded / with empty storage and read the page text: Sign in / Harbor & Thread Support / Email / Password / Sign in. Code: INITIAL_PASSWORD_HASH is a bare constant with no plain-text counterpart anywhere in the repo. I recovered the password from the hash with a short dictionary run (seconds), which also shows the shared demo password is weak. I did not put it in this report.
Problem
Anyone who opens the deployed demo without a private note (a recruiter, a client, your manager's colleague) hits a login wall and cannot see the product at all.
Impact
Portfolio reviewers bounce before seeing a single screen. This is the highest-leverage gap in the project even though the app itself works.
Recommendation
Add a small "Demo accounts" panel under the form listing the lead, agent and developer emails and the shared demo password, ideally with one-click buttons that fill the fields (presentation only; the existing actions.signIn stays as is). Replace the Vite README with a short project README: what it is, how to run it, the demo accounts, and the screens.
Implementation scope
Small
Dependencies
None
Acceptance criteria
A first-time visitor can reach the dashboard in two clicks without reading any other document. README lists run commands and demo accounts.
F-02

Header search loses focus after one character and wipes the open ticket

HighConfirmedP0
Category
Functional
Location
src/components/GlobalSearch.tsx:9-12,30
Current behavior
The search box in PageHeader calls navigate('/tickets?q=…') on every keystroke. Its value is read back from the URL only when the path starts with /tickets.
Evidence
Runtime (headless Chrome): (a) On /dashboard I focused the box and typed "refund" at 120 ms per key. Result: the URL became /tickets?q=r, document.activeElement was BODY, and the value stayed r. (b) On /tickets/TKT-1049?status=in_progress I typed one character in the header box: the URL became /tickets?q=m, the open ticket closed and the status tab reset to All. (c) Typing "refund" on /tickets added 6 history entries (push, not replace). (d) The Tickets page now has two search boxes bound to the same q value. Typing normally on /tickets itself works.
Problem
From any page except Tickets, the primary search accepts exactly one character before the user has to click back into the field, because the first keystroke remounts the header on a different page. From a ticket, it silently drops the open conversation and the status filter. Each key also pollutes browser history, so Back needs many presses.
Impact
Agents searching from the dashboard or a customer page see search "not working". An agent mid-conversation loses their place by searching.
Recommendation
Make the header search submit-driven instead of per-keystroke: keep the typed text in local state, navigate on Enter or the search button (the form already has onSubmit), and use replace when already on /tickets. Preserve existing filter params when on the ticket page. Consider removing the duplicate inbox search or hiding the header box on /tickets, because both edit the same q.
Implementation scope
Small
Dependencies
None
Acceptance criteria
Typing a full word on the dashboard keeps focus and all characters; pressing Enter lands on /tickets?q=word. Searching while a ticket is open does not drop the selected ticket or other filters. One history entry per search.
F-03

Dashboard numbers cannot be acted on, and there is no overdue / unassigned / awaiting queue

HighConfirmedP1
Category
Missing Feature
Location
src/pages/DashboardPage.tsx, src/components/charts.tsx (StatCard), src/components/TicketListPane.tsx
Current behavior
The four KPI cards (13 open, 4 unassigned, 8 awaiting response, 4 past SLA) are plain divs. The Tickets page filters (status, priority, agent, category) cannot express overdue or awaiting-response, and the list sorts only by last update.
Evidence
Runtime: 0 links or buttons inside the four stat cards. The unassigned view exists only through the filter panel or a hand-built URL (/tickets?assignee=unassigned returned the 4 expected tickets). No control anywhere filters to overdue or awaiting-response tickets. Overdue tickets are visible only by scrolling the inbox and spotting a red "Overdue" word.
Problem
A manager can see "4 past SLA" but cannot click through to those four tickets. An agent starting a shift has no one-click queue for "what needs a reply from us right now".
Impact
The dashboard answers "how much work is waiting" but not "which tickets", which is the next question every time. It is the biggest realism gap against tools like Gorgias or Help Scout, which both have views for exactly this.
Recommendation
Make the stat cards links to /tickets with a filter: Open (all active), Unassigned (assignee=unassigned), Awaiting response, Past SLA. Add one filter value view=overdue|awaiting to readFilters/filterTickets using the existing isOverdue and isAwaitingResponse. A row of 4 quick-view tabs above the inbox is the smallest UI; no saved-views system is needed for a team this size.
Implementation scope
Medium
Dependencies
F-04 (agree what "Open" means first)
Acceptance criteria
Clicking "4 past SLA" opens the inbox showing exactly those 4 tickets and the list count matches the card. Same for unassigned and awaiting response.
F-04

"Open" means two different things across the app

MediumConfirmedP1
Category
Data Consistency

src/pages/DashboardPage.tsx:44-45 (Open tickets), src/components/Sidebar.tsx badge, src/components/TicketListPane.tsx (Open tab)
Current behavior
The dashboard card "Open tickets", the sidebar badge and the Tickets page subtitle all count every unresolved ticket (13). The status breakdown and the "Open" tab count only status = open (5).
Evidence
Runtime on seed data: Dashboard Open tickets 13; dashboard By status: Open 5; Tickets tabs All 33 | Open 5 | In Progress 5 | Waiting 3 | Resolved 20; sidebar badge 13; Tickets subtitle "13 active · 20 resolved".
Problem
Two numbers with the same label differ on the same page. A manager comparing the card to the breakdown will think one is wrong. The sidebar badge is also announced as "13 active" but is styled and described elsewhere as open.
Impact
Undermines trust in every metric, which the project explicitly sells as consistent (the code comment in lib/metrics.ts says definitions match everywhere).
Recommendation
Rename the card, badge and subtitle to "Active tickets" (the wording the accessible name and subtitle already use) and keep "Open" strictly for status = open.
Implementation scope
Small
Dependencies
None
Acceptance criteria
No place in the UI uses "Open" for anything other than status = open; the active count is labelled "Active" everywhere.
F-05

Search cannot find order numbers, email addresses or message text

MediumConfirmedP1
Category
Functional
Location
src/lib/filterTickets.ts:31-32
Current behavior
Search matches only the ticket id, subject and customer name.
Evidence
Runtime: ?q=noah returned 3, ?q=TKT-1056 returned 1, but ?q=ORD-10533 returned 0 and ?q=SPRING15 (text from a customer message) returned 0, although ORD-10533 is attached to two tickets. The two placeholders say "Ticket ID, subject or customer", so the behaviour is honest, but it does not match how e-commerce support searches.
Problem
In a store inbox the most common lookup is an order number. A customer who writes "my order ORD-10533" cannot be matched to their ticket by order, and typing their email also returns nothing.
Impact
Slows the most frequent daily task and makes the search look broken when an order id is typed.
Recommendation
Extend the haystack in filterTickets with ticket.orderId and the customer email. Searching message bodies is optional; if added, keep it to the last customer message. Update the two placeholders to list the new fields.
Implementation scope
Small
Dependencies
None
Acceptance criteria
Searching an order id or an email returns that customer's tickets; the placeholder lists the fields searched.
F-06

Demo data ages with the browser, and there is no way to reset it

HighConfirmed (drift simulated)P1
Category
Data Consistency
Location
src/data/seed.ts:407 (buildSeed(now)), src/state/store.tsx:264-295, src/pages/SettingsPage.tsx
Current behavior
Seed timestamps are generated relative to the moment of first load, then persisted in localStorage. There is no "reset demo data" control in Settings or anywhere else.
Evidence
Runtime simulation: I rewound every persisted timestamp by 3 days (equivalent to someone returning after three days) and reloaded. Result: "Awaiting response 8, 8 past SLA" (was 4), the 7-day chart shows zero tickets for Sun, Mon and Tue, notifications read "3 days ago", and 8 of the 33 inbox rows show Overdue. A fresh load showed 4 past SLA and a full chart. The only recovery is clearing site data in dev tools (Settings contains no reset or restore control; confirmed by searching the rendered text).
Problem
Anyone who revisits the demo after a day sees an alarming, empty-looking dashboard that reads as broken rather than "old". Also, once a reviewer experiments (resolves tickets, removes an agent), they cannot return to the starting state.
Impact
First impressions are controlled; second impressions are not. A manager who looks on Monday and shows a client on Wednesday will see different numbers.
Recommendation
Add a "Reset demo data" button in Settings (with the same inline confirm pattern used by Team "Remove") that calls a new settings/resetDemo-style action rebuilding buildSeed(). Optionally rebuild automatically when the saved seed is older than N hours. Keep it explicit that this is demo-only.
Implementation scope
Small
Dependencies
None
Acceptance criteria
After pressing Reset (and confirming), dashboard figures equal a fresh first load. A saved dataset older than the chosen threshold is rebuilt without user action, if that option is taken.
F-07

Seed data contradicts itself on first screen (TKT-1053 and others)

MediumConfirmedP1
Category
Data Consistency
Location
src/data/seed.ts:181-182 (TKT-1053), :124-130 (TKT-1046), src/lib/ticket.ts:46
Current behavior
TKT-1053's thread lists the agent message at 700 min ago before the customer message at 720 min ago (i.e. the customer message is older but stored last). Status logic reads "last array item"; the timeline sorts by time.
Evidence
Runtime TKT-1053: the rendered timeline shows Liam's "Still nothing. I need this for a trip next week." (7:59 AM) before Sofia's "I have escalated to the carrier and offered an expedited reship" (8:19 AM), so the customer appears to complain before the agent's offer. Yet the inbox row and the header both flag the ticket Overdue / "Reply was due 11:59 AM", although the newest message in the rendered timeline is the agent's. Also TKT-1046: subject "Warranty on espresso machine" is attached to ORD-10388, a burr grinder, and the reply talks about the grinder. Ticket created time precedes the first customer message by 50-100 min on several seeds (e.g. TKT-1042), which inflates first-response averages.
Problem
Contradictions are visible within seconds of opening a ticket. The overdue banner contradicts the thread, and the reply is on the wrong side of the customer's complaint.
Impact
Looks like a logic bug in the SLA code when the cause is bad fixture data. It teaches reviewers to distrust the metrics.
Recommendation
Fix the two minute values in the TKT-1053 seed (agent 750, customer 720), correct the TKT-1046 subject or order, and set each ticket's createdMinAgo equal to its first customer message. Add a seed self-check (assert thread minutes are descending) so this cannot recur. Alternatively make isAwaitingResponse sort messages by time before reading the last one.
Implementation scope
Small
Dependencies
None
Acceptance criteria
Opening TKT-1053 shows the customer's "Still nothing" as the last message and an accurate overdue state; no seeded ticket's first message is later than its creation time.

Components are small (largest: store.tsx 393 lines), types are consistent, derived values come from shared functions, and no console errors or lint warnings appear. The items below are the ones that matter for a portfolio read by engineers.

No automated tests, and the reducer holds real business rules

MediumConfirmedP2
Category
Code Quality
Location
package.json scripts, src/state/store.tsx, src/lib/metrics.ts, src/lib/ticket.ts
Current behavior
Scripts are dev, build, lint and preview. No test files exist and no test runner is a dependency. Lint and typecheck both pass cleanly.
Evidence
find for *.test.* and *.spec.* returned nothing. npx oxlint printed no findings; tsc -p tsconfig.app.json --noEmit reported no errors. The bugs in F-07 and F-09 are the kind a small test on isAwaitingResponse and the seed would catch.
Problem
Strongest logic (SLA, metrics, permission checks in the reducer) is unverified, and experienced reviewers look for tests.
Impact
Portfolio credibility with engineers rather than end users.
Recommendation
Add Vitest (it shares the existing Vite config) and test the pure modules only: lib/ticket.ts, lib/metrics.ts, filterTickets, and the reducer's permission and escalation cases. Do not add component tests yet.
Implementation scope
Medium
Dependencies
Adds one dev dependency
Acceptance criteria
npm test runs and passes; at least the SLA, metrics and reducer permission paths are covered.
F-33

Repository polish: template README, favicon 404, unused asset

LowConfirmedP3
Category
Code Quality
Location
README.md, index.html, public/icons.svg

README is the Vite template text. index.html has no icon link although public/favicon.svg exists. public/icons.svg is not referenced.

Runtime console on every load: Failed to load resource: 404 /favicon.ico (the only console error observed in the whole session). grep for icons.svg and favicon in src and index.html returned no references.

Small but immediately visible to developers.

Add <link rel="icon" href="/favicon.svg">, delete or use icons.svg, and replace the README (see F-01).

Small
Dependencies
None

Console is clean on load; README describes the project.

10 · Evidence and reproducible steps

Environment

  • App: Vite 8.3.5 dev server on 127.0.0.1:5199 started from the project folder (read only).
  • Browser: headless Chrome 154 with a clean profile; desktop 1440×900 (also 1280×720, 1280×800, 1024×768, 768×1024) and mobile 390×844 and 320×640.
  • Data: the seeded dataset; tests that changed data were reset by clearing the app's two localStorage keys. Some checks changed data on purpose (a reply, resolve/reopen, an escalation, adding and removing an agent) in that disposable profile only.

Screenshots (all captured from the running app)

  • f-login.png → F-01: Login page as a first-time visitor sees it: no hint of valid accounts.
  • f-dashboard.png → F-03: Dashboard: counts are static cards; "Open tickets 13" sits next to "By status: Open 5".
  • f-stale-dashboard.png → F-06: Simulated return visit three days later: 8 of 8 awaiting tickets past SLA and the last three chart days empty.
  • f-ticket-1053.png → F-07: TKT-1053 (desktop): header warns "Reply was due", while the thread order is out of sequence.
  • f-removed-agent.png → F-11: After removing Hana: reply shown as "Unassigned"; reopened TKT-1045 in the list is already marked Overdue (F-09).
  • f-analytics-14.png → F-14: Last 14 days: cards identical to the 7-day view; first 7 chart days empty; repeated weekday labels.
  • f-tickets-list.png → F-18: Inbox rows: no priority, status or assignee; two Overdue rows are the only urgency signal.
  • f-m-ticket-detail.png → F-26: 390×844: the thread is one clipped bubble; the composer buttons are cut off by the card and nav.
  • f-team-768.png → F-27: 768×1024: page-level horizontal scrollbar (bottom) plus table scrollbar; Workload and Actions are off-screen.
  • f-m-notifications.png → F-28: 390 px: the notification panel starts 15 px off-screen.

Screenshot files are also saved in docs/audit/screenshots/. Screenshots linked to a finding appear inside that finding.

Quick reproduction recipes

  1. F-02: sign in, stay on Dashboard, click the header search, type "refund": only r is kept and focus leaves the field. On /tickets/TKT-1049?status=in_progress type one character: the open ticket closes and the status tab resets.
  2. F-04: compare Dashboard "Open tickets" (13) with "By status → Open" (5) and the Tickets "Open" tab (5).
  3. F-05: open /tickets?q=ORD-10533: 0 results.
  4. F-06: in dev tools, subtract 3 days from every timestamp stored under harbor-thread-support:v1 and reload; the Dashboard shows 8 past SLA and an empty chart tail.
  5. F-07: open /tickets/TKT-1053; the customer's "Still nothing" precedes the agent's offer and the ticket is flagged Overdue.
  6. F-11: as Priya on Team remove Hana Kim, then open /tickets/TKT-1054: her reply is by "Unassigned".
  7. F-14: on Analytics switch between Last 7 and Last 14 days: the cards do not change.
  8. F-20: type in a composer, open another ticket, come back: the text is gone.
  9. F-26: set the viewport to 390×844 and open /tickets/TKT-1053.

13 · Proposed implementation order

  1. Presentation blockers (about half a day): F-01 demo accounts and README, F-33 favicon, F-04 relabel "Open", F-02 header search, F-07 and F-06 seed fixes plus reset button.
  2. Mobile ticket screen: F-26 together with F-19 (one header redesign serves both), then F-28.
  3. Triage and context: F-18 row badges, F-03 clickable KPIs and quick views, F-05 search fields, F-08 customer context strip. These four deliver most of the "feels like a real product" gain.
  4. Make the secondary systems real: F-13 notifications from reducer events, F-12 settings wiring, F-16 developer filter, F-10 assignment hints, F-09 SLA due-in, F-11 author labels.
  5. Analytics credibility: F-14 seed 14 days and fix labels, then F-15 deltas and CSAT card.
  6. Accessibility and quality: F-29 tokens, F-22 chart values, F-30/F-31, F-32 Vitest on the pure modules, F-34 de-duplication.
  7. Optional: F-20 drafts, F-21 templates, F-23-F-25, F-17, F-27.

Nothing here requires a backend, a new framework or a redesign of the existing visual language.

14 · Final portfolio-readiness assessment

DimensionRatingBasis
Core ticket workflowStrongAll reply, note, status, priority, assign, resolve, reopen and escalate paths worked and stayed consistent across views.
Visual consistencyStrongTokens, spacing and components are uniform; minor heading drift (F-25) and contrast (F-29).
Realism for a support teamGoodMissing triage cues, customer context in ticket and search by order (F-18, F-08, F-05).
Data integrity of the demoMixedMetrics reconcile with data, but seeds age and contradict (F-06, F-07).
ResponsiveWeakTicket detail fails on phones; Team overflows on tablets (F-26, F-27).
AccessibilityFairGood labelling basics; contrast, chart access and semantics need work (F-29, F-22, F-30).
Engineering signalsFairClean types and lint; no tests or project README (F-32, F-01).
Verdict: not ready to present unaided; ready after the P0 items. With F-01, F-02 and F-26 resolved the project is a credible, polished small-business support dashboard. Completing the P1 group (triage cues, customer context, quick views, search fields, demo-data reset) would move it from "well-made demo" to "convincing product".

Areas that could not be verified

  • Real touch devices, Safari, Firefox and any screen reader (all runtime checks used desktop Chrome with emulated viewports).
  • Sign-in over plain http on a non-localhost address (F-17), localStorage fully blocked, and two tabs editing the same data.
  • The production build (npm run build not run to avoid overwriting dist/); the existing dist/ is older than the current source.
  • The heavy-workload banner on Team (not triggered by seed data; checked in code only), the assignee dropdown write path (code only), and performance profiling.
  • Whether the weekday-only chart labels confuse users in practice (judged from the 14-day screenshot).

Implementation has not started. Please review the findings and tell me which to apply.
